title: Vocabulary: making decisions and keeping safe
keyIdea: A choice is when you pick what to do. A consequence is what happens because of that choice, and it can be good or bad. A rule tells everyone what to do so we stay safe and are fair. Honest means telling the truth, even after a mistake. Responsible means doing your jobs and looking after things. A trusted adult is a grown-up you know who helps keep you safe; if something feels unsafe, tell one.

kid: A choice is when you pick what to do. Keep the ball, or give it back? A consequence is what happens next. It happens because of your choice. Good choices have consequences too. You give the ball back. Your friend is happy. You grab the cookie. Your brother is cross.
Honest means you tell the truth. Say I broke it, not the cat did it. Then you can fix it with help.
A rule tells us what to do. We hold hands by the road, so we are safe. Fair means everyone gets a turn. Responsible means you do your jobs, like feeding your pet.
Feel unsafe? Tell a trusted adult. That is a grown-up you know, like your teacher, your mum or your grandma. A stranger is not one, even a kind one.
adult: This topic gives five to eight year olds the words for making decisions: choice, consequence, rule, safe, fair, honest, responsible, right and wrong, and trusted adult. Naming the ideas helps children stop and think before they act, and gives them words to talk a choice through with you.

The key link is between a choice and its consequence. Children often think consequence means punishment. Show them that good choices have consequences too, such as a happy friend or easier reading. Ask: what might happen next if you do that?

Common mistakes: thinking only bad choices have consequences; thinking a rule is just to stop fun, not to keep people safe and fair; and thinking telling the truth always gets you in trouble. A key safety slip is thinking that a friendly person is a trusted adult. A trusted adult is someone the child knows who helps keep them safe, such as a parent, a carer, a teacher or a police officer. They should never go with a stranger, however kind.

In the lab your child walks down both roads of a choice to see each consequence, sorts consequences into good and bad, and picks the honest words after a mistake. Then they bring the trusted adults into a safe circle and match the words fair, honest, rule, safe and responsible to pictures.

familyTip: At bedtime, play 'What happens next?': describe a small choice from the day (sharing a toy, leaving a coat at school) and ask what the consequence was. Together, make a list of your child's trusted adults and say their names out loud.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: walk down both roads of a choice, sort consequences, pick honest words, bring trusted adults into the circle and name each picture.

practice.prompt: You share your {n} stickers with a friend. Your friend smiles. What is the smile?
practice.hint: It happened because of your choice.
practice.explain: The smile is a consequence. It happened because you chose to share your {n} stickers. Good choices have consequences too.

practice.prompt: You broke a cup. Which words are honest?
choices: I broke it. I am sorry.
practice.hint: Honest means telling what really happened.
practice.explain: "I broke it. I am sorry" is honest. Blaming the dog or saying it was broken before is not true.

practice.prompt: {n} children want the swing. They each get a turn. What word is that?
practice.explain: It is fair. All {n} children get a turn, with no favourites.

choices: Someone online I do not know
practice.hint: A trusted adult is someone you know, who keeps you safe.
practice.explain: Your teacher is a trusted adult. You know them and they help keep you safe. A stranger is not, even if they seem kind.

choices: What happens because of a choice
pool.hint: Think: choice, then what happens next.
pool.explain: A consequence is what happens because of a choice. It can be good, like a happy friend, or bad, like a fall.

pool.prompt: Why do we have a rule to hold hands by the road?
choices: To keep us safe from cars
pool.hint: What could happen near a busy road?
pool.explain: The rule keeps us safe. Cars are fast, and holding hands stops you running into the road.

pool.prompt: A friendly man you do not know says: come and see my puppy. What do you do?
choices: Say no and tell a trusted adult
pool.hint: Do you know him? Is he a trusted adult?
pool.explain: Say no and tell a trusted adult. Friendly is not the same as trusted. Never go with a stranger.

pool.prompt: Maya feeds her {n} fish every morning without being asked. What is she?
pool.hint: She does her job and looks after her pets.
pool.explain: Maya is responsible. She looks after all {n} fish and does her job every day.

pool.prompt: You leave your coat at the park. It is {n} degrees and you are cold. What is being cold?
pool.hint: It happened because of what you did.
pool.explain: Being cold is a consequence. It happened because you left your coat behind, and {n} degrees is chilly.

pool.prompt: You tell the truth about a mistake. What usually happens?
choices: People trust you and help fix it
You always get in big trouble
pool.hint: Honest words help people trust you.
pool.explain: People trust you and help you fix it. Being honest is right, even when it feels hard.

choices: Wear a helmet on my bike
Ride in the road with no helmet
pool.hint: Which one stops you getting hurt?
pool.explain: Wearing a helmet is safe. It protects your head if you fall. The others could hurt you.
